item.question: A juice vendor has a 5 l container of orange juice. Each glass has a capacity 250 ml. (a): How many full glasses can he serve before the container becomes empty? (b): If he has already served 10 glasses, how much juice is left? (c): If 250 ml of juice is sold at ₹25, how much will he earn by selling 5 l juice?
steps_tex: $(a)$: $5\text{ l}$ is $5,000\text{ ml}$. Each glass holds $250\text{ ml}$. $5,000 \div 250 = 20$ glasses.
$(b)$: $10$ glasses of $250\text{ ml}$ are $10 \times 250 = 2,500\text{ ml}$. The juice left is $5,000 - 2,500 = 2,500\text{ ml}$, which is $2\text{ l}\; 500\text{ ml}$.
$(c)$: $20$ glasses are sold at ₹$25$ each: $20 \times 25 =$ ₹$500$.
Check $(a)$: $20 \times 250 = 5,000\text{ ml}$.

(b): 10 glasses of 250 ml are 10 × 250 = 2,500 ml. The juice left is 5,000 − 2,500 = 2,500 ml, which is 2 l 500 ml.
(c): 20 glasses are sold at ₹25 each: 20 × 25 = ₹500.
